Q: How do I remove the ott number from the end of the species names in my rotl phylogeny plot? A:

You can remove _ott + id from the tree$tip.label using gsub

library(rotl)
(resolved_names <- tnrs_match_names(c("Pongo", "Pan", "Gorilla", "Hoolock", "Homo")))
tr <- tol_induced_subtree(ott_ids = ott_id(resolved_names))
tr$tip.label <- gsub("_ott\\d+", "", tr$tip.label)
plot(tr)

Q: VBA: How can I run a Y-Axis only Min/Max Scale Macro on a Single Line Chart? A:

I recorded the following:

Sub Chart_Max_Y()
'
' Chart_Max_Y Macro
'
    ActiveSheet.ChartObjects("Chart 1").Activate
    ActiveChart.Axes(xlValue).Select
    ActiveChart.Axes(xlValue).MinimumScale = 2
    ActiveChart.Axes(xlValue).MaximumScale = 4
    Application.CommandBars("Format Object").Visible = False
End Sub

Transferring this to your macro should result in:

                End With

Q: Python Plotting Using Class A:

You should define these methods within the class scope, not really important where and in which order. What follows is a quick example:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt    

class Point:
    def __init__(self,x,y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

    def verticalReflect(self,y):
        # your code. an example would be
        dy = y - self.y
        self.y += 2*dy
        return Point(self.x,self.y)

    def translate(self,x,y):
        self.x += x
        self.y += y
        return Point(self.x,self.y)

    def display(self,<options_here>):
        # your code. an example would be
        plt.plot(self.x,self.y,'o',<handle_options>)
        #plt.show()

plt.hold(True)
plt.axis([-10,10,-10,10])
p = Point(2,2)
p.display()
p.translate(3,-1)
p.display()
p.verticalReflect(3)
p.display() 
p.verticalReflect(2)
p.display()
plt.show()

If you omit the <options_here> and <handle_options> parts you have a working example of how to do it. Mind that you can plot and show points immediately within display() method if you uncomment plt.show() call.

I set it up like so, that you call plt.hold(True) first and plot all points on the canvas first, and show all at once only in the last line of code.

I also added the return Point(self.x,self.y) to your code, so you can create new point instead of changing the existing one. If you want to keep the starting point intact you should change self.x|y += ... to x|y += ... and return return Point(x,y).

Best of luck!
